Bambu Lab PLA Tough+Bambu Lab

Sold as toughened or impact-modified: "Engineered for real-world impact, Bambu PLA Tough+ delivers toughness on par with ABS and offers up to 2× stronger layer adhesion than standard PLA. It shrugs off bumps, drops, and hits, making it ideal for RC cars, model planes, and durable tools." (Bambu Lab, PLA Tough+ — official product page, later saved copy, p. 1: Engineered for real-world impact). The maker's statement, not a test result.

  • Good forIt is also cost effective and great for prototyping.BigRep, rPLAp. 1
  • Good forWith spool sizes up to 8 kg, BigRep filaments are optimized for large-scale 3D prints with complex geometries.BigRep, rPLAp. 1
  • BenefitsAs a more sustainable option, BigRep rPLA is a biopolymer made from recycled PLA.BigRep, rPLAp. 1
  • BenefitsEasy to PrintBigRep, rPLAp. 1
  • Pitfalls and limitationsrPLA is not particularly heat resistant.BigRep, rPLAp. 1
  • Pitfalls and limitationsAs with standard PLA, rPLA is not generally considered to have strong resistance to chemicals or UV exposure.BigRep, rPLAp. 1
  • Warping and shrinkagerPLA is affordable, easy-to-use, and with low shrinkage making it great for prototyping, plus it prints well at lower temperatures and high speeds.BigRep, rPLAp. 1
  • Moisture sensitivity50 °C for 4 - 6 hoursBigRep, rPLAp. 1
  • Moisture sensitivityrPLA is a slightly hygroscopic material which means it absorbs moisture from the air which affects the print quality.BigRep, rPLAp. 1
  • Moisture sensitivityWe recommend filament storage with a dryer such as the DRYCON which keeps the filament in perfect condition.BigRep, rPLAp. 1
  • Moisture sensitivityYes, drying rPLA filament is important if it has been exposed to moisture.BigRep, rPLAp. 1
  • Moisture sensitivityrPLA can absorb water from the air resulting in bubbling or stringing while printing with it.BigRep, rPLAp. 1
  • Moisture sensitivityWe recommend using the BigRep DRYCON for 4-6 hours at 50°C, or use any industrial filament dryer or store it in a dry, airtight container with desiccants.BigRep, rPLAp. 1
  • Moisture sensitivityrPLA filament has a long shelf life of 24 months if stored properly in a cool, dry place with minimal exposure to moisture or UV light.BigRep, rPLAp. 1
  • Odour and emissionsYes, it is, as long as the room has good ventilation or an air filtration system for the safety and comfort of the people using the 3D printer.BigRep, rPLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceYes, the BigRep rPLA is compatible with all open material system 3D printers with a heated print bed and adequate temperature extrusion capabilities (200-230°C).BigRep, rPLAp. 1

What the maker says (8)
  • Good forcolorFabb copperFill is a high quality PLA 3D printing filament, loaded with copper particles, specially developed for aesthetic prints.colorFabb, Technical datasheet colorFabb copperFillp. 1
  • Surface finishBy polishing the part, the object will appear with a shiny copper effect, with a statue-like appearance.colorFabb, Technical datasheet colorFabb copperFillp. 1
  • Surface finishSanding and polishing your parts will make the bronze particle shimmer.colorFabb, Technical datasheet colorFabb copperFillp. 2
  • Surface finishStart sanding with sandpaper of grid 120-180.colorFabb, Technical datasheet colorFabb copperFillp. 2
  • Surface finishStart working your way up to sandpaper with grid 240-320, and finish with grit 600 – or higher.colorFabb, Technical datasheet colorFabb copperFillp. 2
  • Surface finishFinally, use a clean soft cloth, and some copper polish.colorFabb, Technical datasheet colorFabb copperFillp. 2
  • Printing adviceDepending on your set-up, 3D printers and slice software, the copperFill requires more flow than normal PLA materials.colorFabb, Technical datasheet colorFabb copperFillp. 2
  • Printing adviceSince copperFill does not exhibit such swelling behavior, it is recommended to decrease the flow rate slightly (4-8% was sufficient for UM2, UM did not need adjustment).colorFabb, Technical datasheet colorFabb copperFillp. 2

  • Pitfalls and limitationsDifficult post-processingPrusa Research, Prusament PLA Recycledp. 1
  • Pitfalls and limitationsIt’s a hard material, but that also means it’s somewhat brittle, and once it breaks, it likes to shatter.Prusa Research, Prusament PLA Recycledp. 1
  • Pitfalls and limitationsThe low print temperature also means low-temperature resistance.Prusa Research, Prusament PLA Recycledp. 1
  • Pitfalls and limitationsParts start to lose mechanical strength at temperatures over 60 °C.Prusa Research, Prusament PLA Recycledp. 1
  • Pitfalls and limitationsThe combination of being both biodegradable and having low-temperature resistance means that it’s not ideal for outdoor use, also due to the low UV-resistance.Prusa Research, Prusament PLA Recycledp. 1
  • Pitfalls and limitationsEven though PLA is biodegradable, and the material on its own is food safe, we suggest not to drink or eat from your 3D prints repeatedly.Prusa Research, Prusament PLA Recycledp. 1
  • Pitfalls and limitationsIt’s because of the small fractures in the print surface, which means bacteria can build up in there over time.Prusa Research, Prusament PLA Recycledp. 1
  • Warping and shrinkageThanks to its minimal thermal expansion, PLA is a great choice for large prints. No warping, no layer separation.Prusa Research, Prusament PLA Recycledp. 1

  • Printing adviceTo achieve the best adhesion of the print surface, it is important to keep it clean.Prusa Research, Prusament PLA Recycledp. 1
  • Printing adviceCleaning the surface is simple: the best option is Isopropyl alcohol ( available in drugstores) which works best not just for PLA, but other materials as well.Prusa Research, Prusament PLA Recycledp. 1
  • Printing advicePour a small amount of IPA on an unscented paper towel and wipe the print surface.Prusa Research, Prusament PLA Recycledp. 1
  • Printing adviceThe bed should be cleaned when it’s cold for the best results but it can also be cleaned when already preheated for PLA, just be careful not to touch the bed surface or the nozzle.Prusa Research, Prusament PLA Recycledp. 1
  • Printing adviceBut keep in mind that when cleaning at higher temperatures, the alcohol will evaporate before it can clean anything.Prusa Research, Prusament PLA Recycledp. 1
  • Printing adviceAlternatively, you can clean the bed with warm water and a few drops of dish soap on a paper towel.Prusa Research, Prusament PLA Recycledp. 1
  • Printing adviceDenatured alcohol is also another option.Prusa Research, Prusament PLA Recycledp. 1
  • Printing adviceWhen post-processing PLA, it’s better to use wet sanding.Prusa Research, Prusament PLA Recycledp. 1
  • Printing adviceWithout water you’ll quickly start heating the plastic by friction, it will melt locally and make it hard to keep sanding.Prusa Research, Prusament PLA Recycledp. 1
  • Printing adviceFeel free to cool PLA during printing as much as possible.Prusa Research, Prusament PLA Recycledp. 1
  • Printing adviceWith good enough cooling you can print extreme overhangs and bridge between far away surfaces.Prusa Research, Prusament PLA Recycledp. 1
  • Printing adviceIf you’re in need of a durable part, increase the number of perimeters rather than increasing the infill percentage as the majority of a 3D print strength comes from its outer shell.Prusa Research, Prusament PLA Recycledp. 1

  • Good forThe pleasant and subtle colors make the rPLA Natural Pigments suitable for various home decor accessories.Prusa Research, Prusament rPLAp. 1
  • Good forFurniture partsPrusa Research, Prusament rPLAp. 1
  • Good forWarm colors perfectly match wooden furniture and allow various designs and functional parts to be made.Prusa Research, Prusament rPLAp. 1
  • Good forToys and visual partsPrusa Research, Prusament rPLAp. 1
  • Good forEasy printability and fast printing allow the making of both large and tiny objects with great looks.Prusa Research, Prusament rPLAp. 1
  • Good forIn general, PLA is used for various aesthetic models, prototypes, and other visual parts.Prusa Research, Prusament rPLAp. 1
  • BenefitsEasy to printPrusa Research, Prusament rPLAp. 1
  • BenefitsCan print huge objectsPrusa Research, Prusament rPLAp. 1
  • Pitfalls and limitationsLow temperature resistancePrusa Research, Prusament rPLAp. 1
  • Pitfalls and limitationsDifficult post-processingPrusa Research, Prusament rPLAp. 1
  • Pitfalls and limitationsThe Prusament rPLA Natural Pigments has mechanical properties similar to regular PLA, but it is slightly more brittle and hygroscopic.Prusa Research, Prusament rPLAp. 1
  • Warping and shrinkageSusceptibility to warping LowPrusa Research, Prusament rPLAp. 1
  • Precision and tolerancePrusament rPLA Natural Pigments is our own in-house made filament with ±0.03mm manufacturing tolerance.Prusa Research, Prusament rPLAp. 1
  • Precision and toleranceCan print tiny partsPrusa Research, Prusament rPLAp. 1
  • Precision and toleranceDetails Under 0.2 mmPrusa Research, Prusament rPLAp. 1
  • Surface finishNice subtle colorsPrusa Research, Prusament rPLAp. 1
  • Surface finishLast but not least, the natural pigments give rPLA pleasant subtle colors , perfectly suitable for various home decor and other aesthetic purposes.Prusa Research, Prusament rPLAp. 1
  • Moisture sensitivityHigher moisture absorbtionPrusa Research, Prusament rPLAp. 1
  • Nozzle wearAbrasivity NonePrusa Research, Prusament rPLAp. 1
  • Odour and emissionsOdor Medium (non-toxic)Prusa Research, Prusament rPLAp. 1
  • Odour and emissionsThe organic additives create a noticeable scent during printing.Prusa Research, Prusament rPLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceTo achieve the best adhesion of the print surface, it is important to keep it clean.Prusa Research, Prusament rPLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceCleaning the surface is simple: the best option is Isopropyl alcohol ( available in drugstores) which works best not just for PLA, but other materials as well.Prusa Research, Prusament rPLAp. 1
  • Printing advicePour a small amount of IPA on an unscented paper towel and wipe the print surface.Prusa Research, Prusament rPLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceThe bed should be cleaned when it’s cold for the best results but it can also be cleaned when already preheated for PLA, just be careful not to touch the bed surface or the nozzle.Prusa Research, Prusament rPLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceBut keep in mind that when cleaning at higher temperatures, the alcohol will evaporate before it can clean anything.Prusa Research, Prusament rPLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceAlternatively, you can clean the bed with warm water and a few drops of dish soap on a paper towel.Prusa Research, Prusament rPLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceDenatured alcohol is also another option.Prusa Research, Prusament rPLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceWhen post-processing PLA, it’s better to use wet sanding.Prusa Research, Prusament rPLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceWithout water you’ll quickly start heating the plastic by friction, it will melt locally and make it hard to keep sanding.Prusa Research, Prusament rPLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceFeel free to cool PLA during printing as much as possible.Prusa Research, Prusament rPLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceWith good enough cooling you can print extreme overhangs and bridge between far away surfaces.Prusa Research, Prusament rPLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceIf you’re in need of a durable part, increase the number of perimeters rather than increasing the infill percentage as the majority of a 3D print strength comes from its outer shell.Prusa Research, Prusament rPLAp. 1

What the maker says (9)
  • Warping and shrinkageUneven heating can lead to unexpected warpage and sub-optimal performance of the partMatterHackers, TECHNICAL DATA SHEET - PRO Series Tough PLAp. 1
  • Warping and shrinkageMeasure dimensions of the part prior to annealing and again after, to determine shrink.MatterHackers, TECHNICAL DATA SHEET - PRO Series Tough PLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceAnnealing can be carried out in an oven or some other medium of heat-transfer, such as a hot water bath.MatterHackers, TECHNICAL DATA SHEET - PRO Series Tough PLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceMeasure temperature at various locations in the oven to ensure absence of hot/cold spots.MatterHackers, TECHNICAL DATA SHEET - PRO Series Tough PLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceTypical time to anneal parts with wall-thickness of 0.125 in (~3.18 mm) is around 20 minutes, but this time is dependent on wall thickness.MatterHackers, TECHNICAL DATA SHEET - PRO Series Tough PLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceFor large dimension parts, it is common to use support fixtures (e.g.-aluminum jigs) during the annealing processMatterHackers, TECHNICAL DATA SHEET - PRO Series Tough PLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceOnce removed from the oven, let the part cool in ambient conditions.MatterHackers, TECHNICAL DATA SHEET - PRO Series Tough PLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceMinimize handling, as inside of the part will likely remain at elevated temperatures longer than the outside.MatterHackers, TECHNICAL DATA SHEET - PRO Series Tough PLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceIf using a water-bath to anneal, the part may have to be at temperature for a slightly longer time to crystallize (since the water-bath cannot be at 110°C-120°C).MatterHackers, TECHNICAL DATA SHEET - PRO Series Tough PLAp. 1

What the maker says (14)
  • Benefits3D-FuelTM Pro PLA (formerly Advanced PLA+/APLA+) Filament is a high heat and impact grade monofilament developed specifically for 3D Printing.3D-Fuel, Technical Data Sheet Pro PLAp. 1
  • BenefitsPro PLA provide excellent 3D printing characteristics such as precise detail, good adhesion to build plates, less warping or curling, and low odor.3D-Fuel, Technical Data Sheet Pro PLAp. 1
  • Pitfalls and limitationsThis grade is not certified for food contact applications.3D-Fuel, Technical Data Sheet Pro PLAp. 1
  • Warping and shrinkageUneven heating can lead to unexpected warpage and sub-optimal performance of the part3D-Fuel, Technical Data Sheet Pro PLAp. 1
  • Warping and shrinkageMeasure dimensions of the part prior to annealing and again after, to determine shrink.3D-Fuel, Technical Data Sheet Pro PLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceIngeo 3D870 is formulated to crystallize when annealed post-printing.3D-Fuel, Technical Data Sheet Pro PLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceCrystallization is a simple and effective route to improve the thermal performance and further enhance the impact properties of Ingeo 3D870.3D-Fuel, Technical Data Sheet Pro PLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceAnnealing can be carried out in an oven or some other medium of heat-transfer, such as a hot-water bath.3D-Fuel, Technical Data Sheet Pro PLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceMeasure temperature at various locations in the oven to ensure absence of hot/cold spots.3D-Fuel, Technical Data Sheet Pro PLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceTypical time to anneal parts with wall -thickness of 0.125 in (~3.18 mm) is around 20 minutes, but this time is dependent on wall thickness.3D-Fuel, Technical Data Sheet Pro PLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceFor large dimension parts, it is common to use support fixtures (e.g.-aluminum jigs) during the annealing process3D-Fuel, Technical Data Sheet Pro PLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceOnce removed from the oven, let the part cool in ambient conditions.3D-Fuel, Technical Data Sheet Pro PLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceMinimize handling, as inside of the part will likely remain at elevated temperatures longer than the outside.3D-Fuel, Technical Data Sheet Pro PLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceIf using a water-bath to anneal, the part may have to be at temperature for a slightly longer time to crystallize (since the water-bath cannot be at 110°C-120°C).3D-Fuel, Technical Data Sheet Pro PLAp. 1
Chemicals and environment (1)
  • Post-processing: described in wordsAnnealing Temperature 110-120°C3D-Fuel, Technical Data Sheet Pro PLAp. 1: Annealing Temperature

What the maker says (11)
  • Good forcolorFabb bronzeFill is a high quality PLA 3D printing filament, loaded with bronze particles, specially developed for aesthetic prints.colorFabb, Technical datasheet colorFabb bronzeFillp. 1
  • Good forColorFabb BronzeFill is a high quality PLA 3D printing filament, loaded with a high amount of bronze particles, especially developed for aesthetic prints.colorFabb, Technical datasheet colorFabb BronzeFillp. 1
  • BenefitsNot only the look and feel that turn these print into art, but in turn also the weight – which is about three to four times heavier than regular PLA(/PHA).colorFabb, Technical datasheet colorFabb bronzeFillp. 1
  • Surface finishPolishing of the printed objects result in a shiny bronze print, with an astonishing statue-like finish.colorFabb, Technical datasheet colorFabb bronzeFillp. 1
  • Surface finishSanding and polishing your parts will make the bronze particle shimmer.colorFabb, Technical datasheet colorFabb bronzeFillp. 2
  • Surface finishStart sanding with sandpaper of grid 120-180.colorFabb, Technical datasheet colorFabb bronzeFillp. 2
  • Surface finishStart working your way up to sandpaper with grid 240-320, and finish with grit 600 – or higher.colorFabb, Technical datasheet colorFabb bronzeFillp. 2
  • Surface finishFinally, use a clean soft cloth, and some copper polish.colorFabb, Technical datasheet colorFabb bronzeFillp. 2
  • Surface finishAfter printing, the objects need to be polished which will result in shiny bronze-like objects.colorFabb, Technical datasheet colorFabb BronzeFillp. 1
  • Printing adviceDepending on your set-up, 3D printers and slice software, the bronzeFill requires more flow than normal PLA materials.colorFabb, Technical datasheet colorFabb bronzeFillp. 2
  • Printing adviceSince bronzeFill does not exhibit such swelling behavior, it is recommended to decrease the flow rate slightly (4-8% was sufficient for UM2, UM did not need adjustment).colorFabb, Technical datasheet colorFabb bronzeFillp. 2

What the maker says (36)
  • Good forThe perfect choice for printing large objects thanks to its low thermal expansion (with little to no warping) and for printing tiny parts because of its low melting temperature.Prusa Research, Prusament PLAp. 1
  • Good forCan print tiny partsPrusa Research, Prusament PLAp. 1
  • Good forCan print huge objectsPrusa Research, Prusament PLAp. 1
  • Good forAction figures often include tons of small features. Printing them with PLA is easy at almost any scalePrusa Research, Prusament PLAp. 1
  • Good forPLA is perfect for printing small and detailed objects, such as jewelry.Prusa Research, Prusament PLAp. 1
  • Good forThanks to its minimal thermal expansion, PLA is a great choice for large prints.Prusa Research, Prusament PLAp. 1
  • Good forThe best use of PLA is for printing concept models, prototypes, miniatures, jewelry, low-wear toys, etc.Prusa Research, Prusament PLAp. 1
  • BenefitsIt’s a very strong and easy to print material.Prusa Research, Prusament PLAp. 1
  • BenefitsHard and toughPrusa Research, Prusament PLAp. 1
  • BenefitsEasy to printPrusa Research, Prusament PLAp. 1
  • BenefitsUnlike so-called thermoset materials, PLA can be heated past its melting point multiple times with very little degradation.Prusa Research, Prusament PLAp. 1
  • Pitfalls and limitationsThe combination of being both low UV resistance and having low-temperature resistance means that it’s not ideal for outdoor use.Prusa Research, Prusament PLAp. 1
  • Pitfalls and limitationsLow temperature resistancePrusa Research, Prusament PLAp. 1
  • Pitfalls and limitationsDifficult post-processingPrusa Research, Prusament PLAp. 1
  • Pitfalls and limitationsIt’s a hard material, but that also means it’s somewhat brittle, and once it breaks, it likes to shatter.Prusa Research, Prusament PLAp. 1
  • Pitfalls and limitationsThe low print temperature also means low-temperature resistance.Prusa Research, Prusament PLAp. 1
  • Pitfalls and limitationsParts start to lose mechanical strength at temperatures over 60 °C.Prusa Research, Prusament PLAp. 1
  • Pitfalls and limitationsThe combination of being both low UV resistance and having low-temperature resistance means that it’s not ideal for outdoor use .Prusa Research, Prusament PLAp. 1
  • Pitfalls and limitationsEven though PLA is the material on its own is food safe, we do not suggest to repeatedly drink or eat from your 3D prints.Prusa Research, Prusament PLAp. 1
  • Pitfalls and limitationsIt’s because of the small fractures in the print surface, which means bacteria can build up in there over time.Prusa Research, Prusament PLAp. 1
  • Warping and shrinkageNo warping, no layer separation.Prusa Research, Prusament PLAp. 1
  • Precision and toleranceWhether it’s a necklace or an earring, you can expect clean edges and no stringing, especially if coupled with a smaller nozzle.Prusa Research, Prusament PLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceUse glue to connect multiple parts together.Prusa Research, Prusament PLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceYou can prevent this by applying a food-safe coating.Prusa Research, Prusament PLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceTo achieve the best adhesion of the print surface, it is important to keep it clean.Prusa Research, Prusament PLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceCleaning the surface is simple: the best option is Isopropyl alcohol ( available in drugstores) which works best not just for PLA, but other materials as well.Prusa Research, Prusament PLAp. 1
  • Printing advicePour a small amount of IPA on an unscented paper towel and wipe the print surface.Prusa Research, Prusament PLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceThe bed should be cleaned when it’s cold for the best results but it can also be cleaned when already preheated for PLA, just be careful not to touch the bed surface or the nozzle.Prusa Research, Prusament PLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceBut keep in mind that when cleaning at higher temperatures, the alcohol will evaporate before it can clean anything.Prusa Research, Prusament PLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceAlternatively, you can clean the bed with warm water and a few drops of dish soap on a paper towel.Prusa Research, Prusament PLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceDenatured alcohol is also another option.Prusa Research, Prusament PLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceWhen post-processing PLA, it’s better to use wet sanding.Prusa Research, Prusament PLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceWithout water you’ll quickly start heating the plastic by friction, it will melt locally and make it hard to keep sanding.Prusa Research, Prusament PLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceFeel free to cool PLA during printing as much as possible.Prusa Research, Prusament PLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceWith good enough cooling you can print extreme overhangs and bridge between far away surfaces.Prusa Research, Prusament PLAp. 1
  • Printing adviceIf you’re in need of a durable part, increase the number of perimeters rather than increasing the infill percentage as the majority of a 3D print strength comes from its outer shell.Prusa Research, Prusament PLAp. 1
